properties.decision:
`cargo test` ABORTS EVERY REMAINING TEST BINARY the moment one fails. This workspace has ~155 of them behind a ~13-minute run, so a change carrying N independent failures cost N FULL CYCLES — fix one, wait, discover the next, wait again. `--no-fail-fast` appeared nowhere: not in AGENTS.md's gate block, not in `ci.yml`. Both now carry it, on both the workspace and core-only gates.

═══ MEASURED, ON THE CHANGE THAT FOUND IT ═══

Adding ONE detector (`quality_target_unstated`, 2026-08-25) took four suite runs. Successive runs reached **31, then 47, then 114 suites** before aborting, surfacing exactly ONE new failure each time:

  run 1  coherence_loop — a "complete design" fixture that had not said what it is for
  run 2  detect.rs ×3   — two fixtures, one over-specific assertion
  run 3  the_surface_says_what_it_already_knew — a truncation counterweight
  run 4  clean

**ALL FIVE WERE IN `reflow2-core`, AND ONE `--no-fail-fast` RUN OF THE CHEAP CORE GATE FOUND THE LAST OF THEM IN SECONDS** — 128 suites, every one executed, the single failure named. That is the same gate that, without the flag, would have stopped at the first.

⭐ THE COST IS REAL AND IT IS THE RIGHT TRADE: a RED run now takes full wall-clock instead of stopping early. But a red run is already a failure, and what anybody wants from it is every fact it holds. A GREEN run is unaffected — it was always going to execute everything.

📌 IT WAS COSTING CI THE SAME WAY, UNSEEN. Every red build was one push-and-wait round per independent failure, and nobody had measured it because each round looked like an ordinary fix.

═══ THE SECOND, SMALLER CAUSE, RECORDED BESIDE IT ═══

The session also skipped its own documented discipline: AGENTS.md says to iterate on `cargo test -p reflow2-core --no-default-features` (seconds) and treat the workspace run as a PRE-PUSH gate. It went from a single new test file straight to the workspace. That turned each iteration into 13 minutes instead of 30 seconds.

🛑 BUT THAT ALONE WOULD NOT HAVE FIXED IT, WHICH IS WHY THE FLAG IS THE ROOT CAUSE AND THE DISCIPLINE IS NOT: the cheap gate fail-fasts too. Following the discipline perfectly would still have revealed one failure per run — faster rounds, the same number of them. Only the flag collapses N rounds into one.

`tools/skill_lint.py` asserts AGENTS.md's gate block and `ci.yml` match FLAG FOR FLAG, so the two cannot drift apart again without turning the build red.
properties.name: DECIDED — the build gate passes `--no-fail-fast`: a red run must yield every fact it has, not the first one
properties.rationale:
Recorded as a Decision rather than left as a commit message because the reasoning is what stops it being reverted by someone who sees a red CI run take longer and reads that as a regression. The trade is deliberate: red runs get slower, and they get complete.

Kept as one node with the discipline failure recorded BESIDE the mechanism rather than instead of it. Blaming the session's shortcut would have produced a resolution nobody can act on ("be more careful") and left the flag missing; naming the flag alone would have lost the true observation that the documented iteration loop was skipped. Both are true and only one is fixable in code.
